items.q: How do offspring from asexual reproduction compare with the parent?
items.misconception: They are genetically different from the parent.
items.random_wrong: They have half the parent's genes.
items.why: Asexual reproduction involves one parent and mitosis, so offspring are clones; sexual reproduction creates variation.

items.q: Is pollination the same as fertilisation?
items.correct: No — pollination is pollen transfer; fertilisation is gametes fusing.
items.misconception: Yes, they are two words for the same event.
items.why: Pollen must first be transferred (pollination); fertilisation is the later fusion of male and female gametes.

items.q: How many chromosomes do gametes have?
items.correct: Half the number of body cells (they are haploid).
items.misconception: The same number as body cells.
items.random_wrong: Twice as many as body cells.
items.why: Gametes are haploid; at fertilisation two gametes restore the full diploid number.

items.correct: From one fertilised egg that splits into two.
items.misconception: From two separate eggs and two sperm.
items.random_wrong: From one egg fertilised by two sperm.
items.why: Identical twins share all genes (one zygote splitting); non-identical twins come from two eggs.
